surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the use of two precursor pairs, SnI4–O2 and SnCl4–H2O2, in an ALD process. The growth mechanism changes with the precursors, and the films are grown by saturating partial surface reactions through alternate dosing of reactants. The films are epitaxially grown on a-Al2O3(0 1 2) substrates, and the surface reactions are controlled to achieve a monolayer thickness control.
evidence: The usefulness of ALD, also referred to as atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), consists in establishing an internal control over the growth by saturating partial surface reactions into which the overall reaction, owing to an alternate and separate dosing of reactants, divides. The films are grown by saturating partial surface reactions through alternate dosing of reactants. The growth mechanism changes with the precursors change. No halogen contamination was found in the 600 8C films down to 0.1%.
